weakness.title: Insufficient Enforcement of One Person per Entry Authorization
weakness.description: The facility does not ensure that an entry authorization admits only the person it was granted to, so additional persons can pass with it.

extended_description.applicability: Controlled entrances where an authorization, such as a badge, a code or a key, is meant to admit a single person, including doors, gates, turnstiles and vehicle entrances. The level of enforcement required depends on the sensitivity of the area behind the entrance.
extended_description.exploitation: A person without authorization enters together with, or immediately behind, an authorized person, with or without that person's consent.

row.details: Unauthorized persons reach information, media and equipment behind the control.
Equipment can be altered by persons who were never authorized.
Access records name the credential holder, not the persons who actually entered.

row.description: Use an entrance that passes a single person for each validation, such as a turnstile, a revolving door or an airlock.
Where passing a single person cannot be enforced, detect a second passage and raise an alert.
Prevent a credential from entering twice without an exit in between.
Tell staff not to hold doors for unrecognized persons, and give them a way to challenge or report.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-3 Physical Access Control
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.2 Physical entry, 7.4 Physical security monitoring
